article.name: Fidelis Memory
article.summary: Fidelis Memory is a local-first Python memory service for coding agents. It stores original passages in a local Chroma vector store, uses configured Ollama embeddings, and exposes bounded retrieval through HTTP and MCP. Its current documented MCP surface supports storage, correction and reads but no record deletion. This review describes source and documentation; runtime quality and resource use were not measured.

who_what.text: The repository identifies Hermes Labs as the project organization and presents Fidelis as a local memory service and client integration for coding agents. It supports MCP, a loopback HTTP API, and a CLI; the agent decides when to call memory tools.
The official Code of Conduct publishes roli@hermes-labs.ai as the project maintainer contact; the exact pinned URL is recorded in contact metadata.

architecture.text: The default store is a local Chroma collection configured under ~/.cogito/store, with Ollama used for embeddings and optional model-backed paths. A service process binds a configured user_id namespace to reads and writes; the code comments say it is not an authenticated identity.

Records keep original text and stable IDs. Temporal writes add service-recorded time and a SHA-256 content hash, plus optional caller-declared event time, validity bounds, source, and superseded IDs. A small SQLite sidecar indexes supersession edges and is rebuildable from vector-store payloads.

behavior.text: The current MCP surface exposes fidelis_store, fidelis_correct, fidelis_recall, fidelis_get, fidelis_recent, and fidelis_health. HTTP /store is verbatim; /add can use optional model extraction. A deterministic gate rejects recognized secret-shaped or obvious noise content. Failed dependency-backed writes may be queued for replay, so queued is not yet stored.

Correction writes a new record that supersedes an existing same-namespace ID; the old passage remains available. Temporal reads annotate current, superseded, expired, and not-yet-valid status, usually retaining historical hits after current results. as_of excludes later-recorded items and later correction links.

The documented MCP and HTTP operation sets contain no record deletion operation. Uninstalling the local service does not delete its store. This review found no supported user-facing fact-delete path in the reviewed public interface.

Fast MCP recall uses bounded local vector search. Zero-LLM recall issues multiple dense subqueries and merges results with reciprocal-rank fusion; thorough retrieval can add BM25 within the dense candidate pool. Optional filter/flagship paths can use configured model endpoints.

Vector searches and ID browse operations apply the configured user_id namespace, but this is local partitioning, not tenant authentication. The security policy states that the HTTP service has no network authentication and is intended for trusted loopback use.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of official docs and selected source files at the verified head. No runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Source presence cannot establish retrieval accuracy, useful save behavior, successful deletion, or safe operation under adversarial inputs.

The official policy says screening recognizes common secret patterns but is not comprehensive; local records are not application-encrypted and the HTTP service must not be exposed to untrusted networks. user_id is not an authorization boundary.

The review did not test backup/restore, concurrent writes, queue recovery, namespace behavior under hostile access, or all client and optional model paths. No documented deletion interface was found; private or future mechanisms were not assessed.

benchmark.note: No Fidelis runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Source and documentation observations are not Fidelis measurements.
